entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gaius Julius Silanus was a Roman senator and general who held a series of offices in the emperor's service. He was suffect consul for the nundinium of January to April 92 as the colleague of Quintus Junius Arulenus Rusticus. Silanus is known solely through inscriptions.





This suffect consulship, though brief, highlights the complex web of power struggles and factional politics within the Roman Senate during the late 1st century AD. Silanus's involvement with Rusticus underscores the shifting alliances and rivalries that characterized the imperial court during this period.





The significance of Silanus's career lies in his ability to navigate the treacherous waters of Roman politics, demonstrating an impressive adaptability and pragmatism in the pursuit of power.
